The Token Behind the Magic: How SAP Scales AI Responsibly
Large SIs (like Accenture, Capgemini) with a formal strategic partnership with SAP. Typically build on behalf of customers rather than packaging reusable products.

A partner company that builds a packaged software product and sells it to many customers. In this context: partners building reusable agents that scale to N customers — the primary target for the North Star.
Open protocol for connecting AI models to external tools and data. The Agent Gateway uses MCP to control every tool call a partner agent makes.
SAP's internal system of record for partner content. UCR feeds MXP; MXP distributes metadata to Discovery Center, Solution Hub, Agent Hub, SAP Work, and SAP.com.
SAP standard for exposing and describing APIs and resources in a machine-readable way. Partners must implement ORD so their agent's capabilities can be discovered and governed by SAP systems.
Partners that implement SAP solutions for customers (e.g. Deloitte, PwC, KPMG). Typically build in the customer's environment; IP stays with the customer.

A specific SAP partner track for ISVs building packaged extensions to SAP solutions. SolEx partners are treated as first-class citizens in the provisioning and commercial model — the North Star starts with them because they already fit SAP's commercial/onboarding structures.
SAP's current provisioning tool for managing tenant subscriptions. Being replaced by URM.
Non-commercial BTP licenses that partners use to build and test their solutions. Cannot be used for customer deployments or sales — productive licenses must be purchased separately.
Part of the Unified Services stack. Handles content and configuration management across the SAP platform.
